summary: Clarion County, PA steel lookout built in 1928 and removed in 1964; a 2012 survey recovery note confirms the tower is gone. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Galvanized steel tower with a watchman's cabin; about 90 ft total height (1928 report); the register calls it a steel Aermotor tower
facts.status_note: Removed in 1964 per the register and Forest Lookouts; a 2012 recovery note on the survey record says the lookout tower has been removed
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters (maintained the tower, per the 1930 report)

events.note: Completed in 1928 and officially designated the Strattonville Fire Tower, per the November 1928 report; register gives 1928
Rotating beacon of 2,000,000 candle power placed on top, per the June 1930 report
Register and Forest Lookouts both give 1964
Survey recovery note credited to Geocaching 2012 says the lookout tower has been removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1928 report gives a 1,600-foot hill, the 1930 report 1,700 feet, and the register 1,503 feet (458 m). The story gives all three and does not choose one.
The 1928 and 1930 reports spell the place Strattonville; the register and the brief use Strattanville. The story uses Strattanville and names the 1928 title once.

notes_for_editor: Status gone is confirmed by two sources (register and Forest Lookouts) and a 2012 survey recovery note. No source describes what is at the site today or whether it is open to visitors, so access is left out of facts. Height 27.4 m is converted from the 1928 report's 'about 90 feet in total height'. The brief's location conflict (Eastern Lookouts coordinates 41.2011, -79.3398) was not visible on the page I read, which prints no coordinates, so it is unverified and the register coordinates are kept. The 1958 survey station description is in the Forest Lookouts page; it places the station about a mile west of town. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 5 page reads plus cached re-greps.
